issue.description:
Per ADR-7: the pipeline container needs Node.js + wrangler (for 'wrangler pages deploy') alongside its existing Python/pyarrow stack, and a way to keep its own current copy of web/ so a data-only deploy always carries current code.

Two parts:
1. Dockerfile changes: add a Node.js runtime (e.g. node:22-slim as an additional stage, or install via apt in the existing python:3.11-slim runtime stage) + 'npm install -g wrangler' (or npx wrangler@latest at call time, matching how the website-build WorkflowTemplate invokes it -- see k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/website-build-workflowtemplate.yml in declarative-config for the exact npx pattern already proven there). Also add git (needed for part 2).
2. Per-cycle web/ refresh: plan.md's ADR-7 explicitly says the pipeline 'keeps its own current copy of web/ (pulled from the repo)' -- NOT baked into the image at build time, so a web/ code change takes effect on the pipeline's next cycle without needing a pipeline image rebuild. Implement this as a shallow git clone (git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jedarden/hetzner-auction-dashboard.git, public read-only, no auth needed) of just the web/ subdirectory at the start of each cycle (or cached + git pull if unchanged -- implementer's call, either is fine as long as it's fresh each cycle, not stale from container startup).

Acceptance criteria:
- Built image can run 'wrangler --version' and 'git --version' successfully
- A full pipeline cycle (against a scratch/test Cloudflare Pages project, or mocked) shows web/'s files present in the assembled deploy directory and reasonably current (not just whatever was baked in at image build time)
- Image size/build time stays reasonable for a personal project -- no need to optimize hard, just don't blow past what iad-ci's kaniko build step can handle in its resource limits (see hetzner-auction-pipeline-build-workflowtemplate.yml)

issue.description:
_parse_disks in pipeline/src/pipeline/fetcher.py currently expects a flat disks/storage/drives list or legacy hdd_count/hdd_size_gb fields -- none of which exist in the real feed. Full schema + worked example in docs/notes/hetzner-live-feed-schema-2026-08-06.md.

Real shape: item['Hardware']['Storage']['Details'] is a dict with keys hdd, sata, nvme (each a flat list of per-disk capacity-in-GB integers, one entry per physical disk) plus a redundant general key (ignore it -- it's a flattened union of the other three, not a fourth type).

Rewrite _parse_disks to:
- Map hdd->"HDD", sata->"SSD" (Hetzner's SATA auction drives are SSDs, not spinning disks -- confirmed against Details.Information's human-readable strings), nvme->"NVMe".
- Group each type's flat capacity list into DiskSpec(type, count, capacity_gb) by identical capacity value -- e.g. hdd:[6000,6000] -> one DiskSpec(HDD, count=2, capacity_gb=6000). A type with differing capacities (e.g. sata:[500,250]) emits one DiskSpec per distinct capacity -- this already matches plan.md Data Models' 'one struct per distinct disk type/size group' rule, no plan change needed.
- Remove the old dead fallback branches entirely (item.get('disks')/'storage'/'drives' dict/list parsing, legacy hdd_count/hdd_size_gb fields) -- none of them correspond to anything the real feed sends; per house convention, delete confirmed-dead code rather than leaving it as defensive cruft.

Acceptance criteria:
- A listing with all three disk types present in different capacities (see the mixed-disk example in the notes file: nvme:[960,960], hdd:[6000,6000]) parses into exactly 2 DiskSpec entries (NVMe count=2 capacity_gb=960, HDD count=2 capacity_gb=6000).
- A single-disk-type listing (e.g. sata:[250,250], nvme/hdd empty) parses into exactly 1 DiskSpec.
